paragraphs: Friend, the water went down, but people didn't get reset. Noah drinks some wine, becomes drunk and uncovers himself inside his tent, and I think that's a heavy moment (Genesis 9:21). Then the brothers split. Ham "told his two brothers outside," while Shem and Japheth "took a garment" and covered their father (Genesis 9:22-23).

Here's what I take from it. Somebody's lowest moment lands in your hands, and you get to choose: forward it to the group chat, or grab a blanket and cover them. Shem and Japheth even walk in backward so they don't see (Genesis 9:23). I trip over my own base walking forward, so that's a serious commitment, but I'd pick the garment every time.

Then Genesis 10 rolls out name after name, clan after clan, and wraps up with this: "From these the nations of the earth spread out after the flood." (Genesis 10:32). Even with a family this messy, the whole earth was populated from Noah's three sons (Genesis 9:19). So when somebody's mess lands in your hands, baker, don't broadcast it. Cover it, and trust God to keep writing the story.
